jobs.title: Deputy Director
jobs.description:
Hospitality House is an emergency shelter and housing provider serving low\-income and homeless residents in Nevada County. Hospitality House provides pathways to housing by bringing homeless residents into a compassionate circle of community care that offers shelter, housing resources, sustenance, opportunity, dignity, and hope as they transition from homelessness to housing.

We are seeking a strategic, mission\-driven Deputy Director to help lead our organization into its next chapter. This is a rare opportunity to step into a senior executive role with a clear, intentional pathway to the Executive Director position working side\-by\-side with our current Executive Director to shape agency strategy, strengthen programs, and build lasting community partnerships. If you are a seasoned nonprofit leader ready to grow into an executive director role while making a tangible difference for people experiencing homelessness in the Sierra Foothills, we invite you to apply.

Rate of Pay

$120,640 – $124,800 annually

**Benefits**

* Medical Insurance (100% of premium paid by the employer).
* Dental Insurance.
* Vision Insurance.
* Life Insurance.
* Long\-term Disability Insurance.
* Voluntary Short\-term Insurance.
* Voluntary Accident.
* Voluntary Critical Illness.
* 401k.
* 11 paid holidays.
* 11 paid sick days.
* Paid vacation days

**POSITION SUMMARY**

Hospitality House seeks a full\-time Deputy Director to help manage the day\-to\-day operations of the organization alongside the Executive Director. The Deputy Director is a senior executive\-level role providing strategic, operational, and programmatic oversight in close partnership with the Executive Director. The Deputy Director will directly supervise the Housing and Supportive Services Officer, the CalAIM Manager, and the Development team, while supporting programmatic divisions to ensure high\-quality services, regulatory compliance, and mission alignment. When needed, the Deputy Director will serve as the Acting Executive Director.

This role is intentionally structured as a succession pathway to the Executive Director position. The Deputy Director will receive mentorship and hands\-on training in governance, development, financial stewardship, human resources, and operations to build readiness to assume full organizational leadership.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Leadership and Visioning**

* Partner with the Executive Director to design and implement the strategic framework that upholds Hospitality House's values, mission, and vision.
* Serve as a visible ambassador of the agency in community, regional, and state\-level collaborations, task forces, and public forums.
* Keep abreast of evolving best practices in homelessness services, program design, and regulatory compliance, bringing innovation back to the agency.

**Programmatic Oversight and Personnel Management**

* Provide direct supervision and mentorship to the Housing and Supportive Services Officer, CalAIM Manager, and Development Director, as well as other applicable staff.
* Ensure case management, shelter, outreach, and housing programs are delivered in alignment with best practices, contractual requirements, and agency standards.
* Support staff recruitment, training, and retention efforts to ensure consistent service quality.
* Partner with HR in staff development planning; conduct regular performance evaluations and recommend recognition/reward as appropriate.

**Grants, Contracts, Database Management, and CalAIM Compliance**

* Collaborate with the Director of Business Operations and other members of leadership to ensure effective data collection, reporting, and compliance for grants and contracts.
* Partner with Business Operations to monitor program budgets, reimbursements, and regulatory reporting obligations.
* Participate in proposal development and reporting processes to strengthen funding streams.

**Community Relations**

* Represent Hospitality House in collaborative partnerships with service providers, local government, funders, donors, and community stakeholders.
* Actively participate in education, outreach, and advocacy efforts to raise awareness of homelessness and the organization's impact.
* Strengthen Hospitality House's public profile by cultivating strong relationships with civic leaders, business partners, faith communities, and philanthropists.

**CalAIM Program Oversight**

* Provide leadership oversight of Hospitality House's CalAIM Program, ensuring compliance with state and federal regulations, contract requirements, and organizational policies.
* Supervise and support the CalAIM Manager, ensuring accurate and timely billing, audits, reporting, and data management.
* Partner with Business Operations, HR, and program leadership to ensure CalAIM staff are trained, resourced, and compliant with evolving CalAIM standards.
* Monitor performance and quality metrics, ensuring CalAIM services are delivered effectively, efficiently, and in alignment with best practices.
* Serve as a liaison with managed care plans, funders, and state/local agencies regarding CalAIM implementation and compliance.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director and leadership team to integrate CalAIM program outcomes into broader organizational strategy, sustainability planning, and funding requests.

**Fundraising and Development**

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non\-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions\-driven, passionate change\-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world\-wide for a better future.


We are committed to a culture of bold leadership, innovation in all aspects of our work, creative partnerships and, most crucially, accountability to those we serve. We are a dedicated advocate for the most vulnerable.

**Job Overview:**  

As the Development Director you will oversee the design, implementation, and monitoring of resource mobilization efforts in support of our mission. The specific areas of responsibility and oversight include: donor relations and reporting, collaboration with colleagues at IRC headquarters on a new collaborative fundraising structure for individual donors, outreach and prospecting to local corporate and private foundation donors, special events planning and oversight. As a member our region's senior leadership team, you will share responsibilities with other Directors for providing effective oversight over regional operations and good stewardship of resources. This is a full\-time exempt position, reporting to the Executive Director of the Sacramento/Turlock region.

**Major Responsibilities:**  

The Development Director works in close coordination with the Executive Director and local leadership to achieve the following goals:

* Develop and implement an annual fundraising plan with specific and measurable goals and objectives for development of restricted and unrestricted funds.
* Develop strategy for and execute special, restricted fundraising campaigns through digital and traditional channels, in partnership with HQ Mass Markets teams.
* Cultivate national partnerships from companies and foundations based in the Sacramento/Central Valley region, in coordination with HQ\-based Institutional Philanthropy \& Partnerships team.
* Support local high\-value donor qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship in close collaboration with USA Philanthropy team.
* Oversee the preparation of letters of inquiry, proposals, budgets and reports to local foundations and other potential donors in coordination with the Sacramento\-Turlock grants team, office leadership and HQ counterparts.
* Oversee joint initiatives with local programming to identify funding needs and create strategic plans to seek funding support for these needs.
* Organize annual fundraisers and other special events as applicable.
* Ensure development of strong corporate donor engagement opportunities that are aligned with program need and donor interest for national and local donors.
* Serve as focal point and liaison for Sacramento\-Turlock to HQ fundraising teams.
* Provide high level oversight for the Sacramento\-Turlock grants team.
* Coordinate with Resource \& Development Coordinators across the region to ensure consistency between volunteer and financial / in\-kind support.
* Assist in raising awareness about the IRC and representing the office at meetings, seminars, and forums.
* Recruit, hire, train and supervise development\-related interns and volunteers, when appropriate.
* Maintain ongoing communication on status of resource development initiatives and provide timely reports on management issues and concerns.
* Participate actively on Sacramento\-Turlock’s Leadership Team and collaborate closely with management team to ensure efficient collaboration with all offices in the delivery of quality services
* Work with Executive Director on opportunities to highlight the local and global work of IRC.
* Other tasks as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

* University degree (BA/BS) required; graduate degree in Development, Nonprofit Management or Business Management, or International Relations preferred
* Minimum of five (5\) years prior experience with leading fundraising, communications, public relations, and other development duties in the non\-profit sector required
* Impeccable attention to detail
* Experience with Salesforce strongly preferred
* Strong writing skills required
* Strong donor network in the Sacramento/Central Valley region preferred
* Demonstrated record of foundation and donor relations with successful development of private foundation grant proposals
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively and diplomatically with donors, volunteers, partner agencies, government officials, multi\-cultural clients and colleagues on all levels. Demonstrated ability to work successfully in a multi\-cultural environment.
* Experience coordinating multiple partners and consensus building toward common goal.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (especially Word, Excel, Outlook) and internet research
* Strong organizational, leadership and team\-building skills with ability to promote productivity and efficiency

**Working Environment:**


Hybrid work with minimum 3x/week in office. Standard office environment. Some travel to other regional offices required as well as to various venues for events and for meeting with donors. Availability for non\-traditional hours including weeknights and weekends on a limited basis required.  

  

**Compensation:** ($109,416 \- $117,354\). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience

**About Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay**

Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to build decent, affordable homes and provide home ownership opportunities to qualified families who live and work in Santa Cruz and Monterey Counties. Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is an independent, locally operated and funded affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development is the affiliate's senior fundraising leader and a member of the leadership team, working in close partnership with the Chief Executive Officer and the Board of Directors, responsible for leading Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay's fundraising, donor engagement, and development operations. This role secures philanthropic revenue, cultivates donor relationships, oversees fundraising campaigns, and implements strategic development initiatives that advance the organization's mission \- working across individual, corporate, foundation, faith, public, and in\-kind sources.

This position requires strong relationship\-building skills, strategic thinking, and a commitment to driving sustainable revenue growth in support of Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay's mission. The right candidate is a self\-starter who can set direction and execute it, is as comfortable with a database and dashboard as with a donor meeting, and is energized by working across every giving sector rather than specializing in one. The Director also supervises and mentors the Fundraising and Development Manager, building a small, high\-functioning development team.

**Primary Duties \& Responsibilities: Fundraising \& Revenue Development**

* Plan, implement, and manage annual fundraising strategies to meet organizational revenue goals
* Develop an annual development plan with revenue targets by source, aligned with the affiliate's strategic plan, operating budget, and construction schedule; report progress to the CEO monthly and to the Board as its Development Committee regularly.
* Participate in all aspects of the gift cycle from initiating contacts through stewardship.
* Meet specific annual fundraising goals and contact metrics set by the Chief Executive Officer.
* Lead donor cultivations, solicitation, and stewardship efforts, including individual giving, major donors, and monthly donor programs. Personally manage a portfolio of major and mid\-level donors and partner with the CEO and Board members on principal\-gift strategy, joint cultivation, and solicitations, preparing them for donor meetings and accompanying them on calls.
* Establish or strengthen a planned giving program and legacy society.
* Develop and execute online fundraising initiatives and seasonal appeals.
* Secure and strengthen corporate and community employee volunteer partnerships with regional employers, financial institutions, homebuilders, and suppliers.

**Donor \& Community Engagement**

* Steward donors through personalized communication, meetings, and engagement activities.
* Oversee donor recognition initiatives and maintain accurate records in the organization's donor database (Bloomerang).
* Plan and coordinate fundraising events, community fundraising, and donor appreciation events.
* Coordinate with construction and volunteer staff so that build\-site engagement converts to sustained financial partnerships; grow in\-kind giving and ReStore donor relationships in coordination with ReStore leadership.
* Collaborate with program staff to develop compelling proposals, reports, and presentations for donors.
* Support organization\-wide events, outreach efforts, and public communications as needed.
* Serve as a visible ambassador for the affiliate at community, civic, and industry events.

**Board \& Volunteer Engagement**

* Staff the Board's Development Committee; equip Board members with tools, training, and prospect assignments so that every member participates meaningfully in fundraising.
* Serve as a strategic partner to the CEO and Board Chair on fundraising strategy, donor relationships, and the Board's role in resource development; provide regular briefings so that Board members are informed, confident, and equipped to open doors.
* Recruit, organize, and steward fundraising volunteers and event committees.

**Staff Leadership \& Mentoring**

* Supervise, coach, and mentor assigned staff and foster a collaborative culture of philanthropy across staff, volunteers, and the Board, so that everyone in the organization sees a role in resource development.

**Administrative \& Organizational Support**

* Analyze donor data to tailor fundraising approaches.

* Manage the development budget and ensure gift acceptance, donor privacy, and recognition policies are current and consistently applied.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

jobs.description:
Education Program Director, Greater Good Education \#88470 About Berkeley
  
  

At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation \- driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  

At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full\-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  

We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  

Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  

Departmental Overview
  
  

The Greater Good Science Center at UC Berkeley (GGSC) studies the psychology, sociology, and neuroscience of well\-being and teaches skills that foster a thriving, resilient, and compassionate society. Over more than two decades, the GGSC has provided a bridge between scientists and the public, turning research findings into practical resources that support well\-being for all. Since its founding, the Center has highlighted the importance of building social connections not only within communities but across groups, offering practical strategies for overcoming bias and prejudice, expanding one's circle of care, and promoting diversity, inclusion, and belonging.
  
  

The GGSC's Greater Good Education (GGE) program provides education professionals with practical, scientific insights to help them integrate the science of well\-being and flourishing into their lives, schools, and classrooms. It draws on disciplines such as social\-emotional learning, mindfulness, character education, and related topics. GGE's goal is to help education professionals better understand the roots of kind, helpful \- or "prosocial" \- behavior and emotional well\-being, and how they can build those skills in themselves, their colleagues, and their students.
  
  

GGE resources include our pioneering Greater Good in Education website, which offers more than 350 actionable, research\-based practices and has engaged several million users; a suite of online courses that support student and educator well\-being; Greater Good articles that share the latest education\-related research and its practical application in classrooms and schools; and Greater Good Educators, a community of practice program that brings together educators from around the world to learn with and from each other about the keys to individual and collective well\-being in education.
  
  

The GGSC's organizational culture prioritizes independence, rigor, and the well\-being of its members. Staff members enjoy autonomy and flexibility while working in a culture that encourages teamwork, connection, and collaboration. The GGSC welcomes a diversity of experiences and perspectives to inform its work and strives to operate internally by the values that drive its public\-facing programs: empathy, compassion, joy, forgiveness, appreciation, and cooperation. Recognizing that the science we cover has been shaped by systemic biases and inequities, we aim to address and correct for these prejudices whenever possible.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

This position serves as the Greater Good Education (GGE) Program Director, overseeing the program's mission to build kinder, happier schools where everyone belongs. This position leads the short\- and long\-term planning for GGE, shaping the program's goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model. Working closely with the GGSC's executive director, the Education Program Director manages fundraising for the program and ensures that the program's direction aligns with the GGSC's overall direction. This position supervises a team that includes the Associate Director, Program Coordinator, Director of Learning Communities, Director of Educational Partnerships, Marketing Specialist, and Communications Specialist.
  
  

The Education Program Director oversees all GGE program content, partnerships, and other activities, including training, evaluation, and communities of practice, while also overseeing the development of the new Greater Good Schools program, which focuses on integrating Greater Good values into the fabric of entire schools and districts. The successful candidate possesses extensive experience in K\-12 education and a strong grasp of the science of social\-emotional learning, mindfulness, character development, and other prosocial research in education. Additionally, this position requires an entrepreneurial spirit and a command of nonprofit strategy, development, and management.
  
  

Application Review Date
  
  

The First Review Date for this job is September 22, 2026\. For full consideration, please apply by the first review date.
  
  

Responsibilities
  
  

Lead Program Strategy and Development
  
  

Lead short\- and long\-term strategic planning for Greater Good Education (GGE), shaping the program's goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model, in collaboration with the GGSC's executive director and GGE program staff.
  
Identify and pursue funding opportunities for GGE, working in concert with the GGSC's executive director, deputy director, and development director.

**ORGANIZATION OVERVIEW**

Founded in October of 1995, United Samaritans Foundation mission is to deliver food to people in need in Stanislaus County, and to facilitate the provision of services to assist them in a transition to a better quality of life.

In today’s economy, with housing costs, utilities and groceries climbing, earning a wage is no longer a guarantee of having enough to eat. United Samaritans Foundation serves the gap between what people earn and what life costs.

Revenues: $ 1\.9 million\~. For more information please visit: unitedsamaritans.org

**POSITION DESCRIPTION** 

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight for all organizational activities, ensuring alignment with the mission and vision.
* Serve as the primary representative of the organization to community partners, donors and the community.
* Develop and implement operational policies, procedures, and best practices to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.
* Lead, motivate, and manage staff by providing guidance while delegating responsibilities appropriately.
* Oversee program development, expansion, and evaluation to ensure high\-quality service delivery.
* Collaborate closely with the Board of Directors to establish organizational goals, monitor progress, and report on performance.
* Foster a positive organizational culture that encourages innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with all legal, regulatory, and funding requirements.
* Drive fundraising efforts in partnership with development staff to support organizational sustainability.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Proven experience in executive leadership or senior management roles within a nonprofit or similar organization.
* Strong strategic thinking skills with the ability to develop and execute long\-term plans.
* Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills to effectively engage diverse stakeholders.
* Demonstrated ability to lead teams, delegate responsibilities effectively, and build a collaborative work environment.
* In\-depth knowledge of organizational operations, program management, and industry\-specific best practices.
* Ability to develop a thorough understanding of the organization’s core programs and operational landscape.
* Experience working with a Board of Directors or governing body is preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in nonprofit management, public administration or related field is advantageous.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS** 

Successful candidates for this position will undergo background checks. Applicants will have an opportunity to discuss any adverse background information before a determination is made about its potential impact on their candidacy.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**

The salary range for this position begins at $85,000 yearly, based on education and experience. The total compensation package includes health benefits, and 6 paid holidays.

**HOW TO APPLY**

To apply, submit a resume and cover letter. Your resume must not exceed two (2\) pages and should demonstrate how your experience meets the minimum qualifications for the position. Your cover letter must not exceed two (2\) pages and should describe why you are interested in the position and how your professional, education and personal experiences meet the desired attributes listed above.

For questions about the position or the application process or accommodations, please contact Linda at 209\.668\-4853 or email to: Linda@unitedsamaritans.org.

Pay: From $85,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

Work Location: In person

As the chapter’s principal external leader, the Executive Director will elevate the Red Cross presence across Orange County—engaging donors, volunteers and community partners to advance humanitarian impact and long\-term resilience.

**CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER (COO)**

**G\&G Garage Door Co. \| Torrance, California**

**$150,000–$200,000 Annual Salary \+ Performance Incentives**

**HELP US BUILD A $25 MILLION COMPANY**

G\&G Garage Door Co. is seeking an **experienced, high\-performing Chief Operating Officer (COO)** to help lead our company through its next major stage of growth.

We are currently a **$10–$12 million annual revenue company**, and our next goal is clear:

**SCALE G\&G GARAGE DOORS TO $25 MILLION\+ IN ANNUAL REVENUE.**

We are looking for a COO who has the experience, leadership ability, financial understanding, and operational discipline to help us get there — **without sacrificing profitability, customer experience, quality, or company culture.**

**Salary: $150,000–$200,000 annually, based on experience and proven results, with additional performance\-based incentive opportunities.**

This is not a position for someone looking to become a COO for the first time.

**We are looking for someone who has successfully done this before.**

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

G\&G Garage Doors has established a strong business and reputation in the Southern California and San Francisco markets.

We aren't looking for someone to simply maintain what we've built.

**We're looking for an experienced operator who can help us double it.**

You will work directly with ownership to develop and execute the operational strategy necessary to grow the company from approximately **$10–$12 million to $25 million\+ in annual revenue.**

That means building the people, systems, processes, accountability, leadership structure, and operational capacity required to support significant growth.

**THE POSITION**

As COO, you will have significant responsibility for the operational performance of the company, including:

* Overall day\-to\-day operations
* Revenue growth and operational capacity
* Profitability and margin improvement
* Service and installation departments
* Sales performance and conversion
* Customer service and call center performance
* Dispatching and scheduling
* Recruiting and workforce planning
* Employee training and development
* Manager development and accountability
* KPI development and performance scorecards
* P\&L management
* Budgeting and forecasting
* Inventory and purchasing controls
* Quality control and callback reduction
* Standard operating procedures
* Technology and process improvement
* Customer satisfaction
* Company culture
* Building a scalable leadership structure

**WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

Our ideal COO has already helped grow a company through a similar stage of development.

**We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience taking a business from approximately $10M in revenue to $20M, $25M, $30M or beyond.**

Strong candidates will have:

* Previous experience as a **COO, VP of Operations, President, General Manager, or comparable senior executive**
* A proven track record of scaling a multimillion\-dollar business
* Experience managing multiple departments and department leaders
* Strong P\&L and financial management experience
* Experience managing labor, margins, productivity, and profitability
* A strong understanding of KPIs and performance management
* Experience building systems and processes that support rapid growth
* Experience recruiting and developing high\-performing managers
* The ability to hold teams accountable while maintaining a positive culture
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving abilities
* Excellent communication and leadership skills

**HOME\-SERVICE EXPERIENCE IS HIGHLY PREFERRED**

Experience in businesses such as:

**Garage Doors**  HVAC **Plumbing**  Electrical **Roofing**  Construction **Home Improvement**  Field Services **Other Residential Service Businesses**

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**

Your mission is bigger than simply increasing revenue.

We want to build a **stronger, more profitable, more scalable company.**

Success will include:

§ **$25M\+ Revenue**

§ **Healthy \& Improving Profitability**

§ **Strong Gross Margins**

§ **Higher Technician Productivity**

§ **Improved Sales Conversion**

§ **Strong Booking Rates**

§ **Efficient Labor Utilization**

§ **Reduced Callbacks**

§ **Exceptional Customer Satisfaction**

§ **Strong Employee Retention**

§ **Accountable Department Leaders**

§ **Predictable Operational Performance**

**YOUR FIRST PRIORITY**

Before trying to change everything, we expect our COO to understand the business.

· Learn about our people.

· Learn our customers.

· Understand our numbers.

· Identify what's working.

· Identify what's holding us back.

Then develop a clear operational roadmap for taking G\&G Garage Doors from approximately **$10–$12 million to $25 million\+ in annual revenue.**

We want a COO who can create that plan — and then lead the organization in executing it.

**COMPENSATION**

**Base Salary: $150,000–$200,000 Per Year**

Compensation will be determined based on experience, previous accomplishments, and demonstrated ability to scale an organization.

We also believe exceptional performance should be rewarded.

The position may include a **significant performance\-based incentive/bonus opportunity** tied to measurable company objectives such as:

* Revenue growth
* EBITDA / profitability
* Gross margin improvement
* Operational efficiency
* Customer satisfaction
* Employee retention
* Achievement of company growth milestones

For the right person who helps us successfully build a $25M\+ organization, **there should be meaningful upside.**

**This is an opportunity to join an established company at an exciting point in its growth.**

**The foundation is already here.**

**The opportunity is here.**

**Now we need the operational leader who can help us build the next version of G\&G Garage Door Co.**

jobs.title: Senior Director of Development
jobs.description:
**Position Category:** Staff (Exempt)
  
**FLSA:** Exempt
  
**FTE:** 1
  
**Location:** Thousand Oaks
  
  

**University Background:**  

The mission of California Lutheran University is to educate leaders for a global society who are strong in character and judgment, confident in their identity and vocation, and committed to service and justice. Founded in 1959 in beautiful Ventura County, the university has an enrollment of about 4,000 undergraduate and graduate students who come from across the nation and around the world from a diversity of backgrounds, cultures and faiths. As a federally recognized Hispanic\-Serving Institution, Cal Lutheran is looking for candidates with a dedication to and success in working in diverse communities. The university is committed to an inclusive learning and work environment that values individual differences and respects each person's dignity.
  
  

**Basic Function:**  

Reporting to the Vice President for Growth \& Advancement, the Senior Director of Development is responsible for identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major gift prospects and donors in support of the University's fundraising priorities. The position manages an assigned portfolio of major gift prospects and donors and develops individualized strategies to advance relationships through qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  
  

The Director serves as the primary Advancement point person for Athletics fundraising, working collaboratively with other fundraisers and campus partners. The position also supports fundraising efforts involving parents and other University priorities as assigned.
  
  

**Representative Duties:**  

Manage an active portfolio of approximately 75\-150 major gift prospects and donors, developing and maintaining individualized plans to advance relationships through qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  
Identify, cultivate, and solicit major gifts and principal gifts, in support of University fundraising priorities.
  
Conduct substantive donor and prospect meetings and travel as needed to develop relationships and advance gift opportunities.
  
Collaborate with the Vice President for Growth \& Advancement and Associate Vice President for Advancement in developing and implementing fundraising strategies for Athletics and parents.
  
Serve as the primary Advancement point person for Athletics fundraising, working with Athletics leadership, coaches, Advancement colleagues, and other campus partners to identify prospects, funding priorities, and philanthropic opportunities.
  
Coordinate with other Advancement fundraisers to support a collaborative approach to Athletics fundraising and donor engagement.
  
Work with University administrators, faculty, staff, and other campus partners to understand institutional and departmental funding priorities and connect donor interests with appropriate giving opportunities.
  
Prepare and present gift proposals, correspondence, and other fundraising materials aligned with donor interests and University priorities, including proposals for corporate and foundation prospects as appropriate.
  
Identify planned and blended giving opportunities and collaborate with appropriate Advancement colleagues and subject\-matter experts as needed.
  
Maintain accurate and timely donor and prospect records, including contact reports, proposal status, and other moves management activity, in the University's CRM.
  
Monitor and report progress toward established portfolio and fundraising goals and performance expectations.
  
Work with Advancement colleagues to identify and qualify alumni, parents, friends, and other prospective donors based on philanthropic interest and giving potential.
  
Collaborate with colleagues across University Advancement, including annual giving, planned giving, advancement operations, stewardship and donor relations, and alumni engagement, to coordinate donor activities and relationships.
  
Engage volunteers as appropriate and participate in donor cultivation, stewardship, fundraising, Athletics, and University events and programs.
  
Maintain current knowledge of major and planned giving practices, charitable giving vehicles, and relevant fundraising trends.
  
Maintain confidentiality and adhere to University policies, professional fundraising standards, and applicable laws and regulations.
  
Perform other related duties as assigned.
  
  

**Knowledge Of:**  

Major gift fundraising principles and practices.
  
Donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  
Major gift portfolio and moves management.
  
Donor relationship management and prospect development.
  
Fundraising proposals and donor communications.
  
Higher education or nonprofit advancement practices.
  
Planned and blended giving concepts and charitable giving vehicles.
  
Advancement CRM systems and donor records.
  
Professional and ethical standards related to fundraising and donor confidentiality.
  
  

**Ability To:**  

Cultivate, solicit, and steward major gift prospects and donors.
  
Manage an assigned portfolio and consistently advance donor relationships.
  
Build effective relationships with donors, prospects, alumni, parents, volunteers, University leadership, faculty, staff, Athletics personnel, and other constituents.
  
Connect donor interests with University funding priorities and philanthropic opportunities.
  
Prepare and present effective gift proposals and donor communications.
  
Collaborate effectively with Advancement colleagues and campus partners.
  
Exercise sound judgment, discretion, diplomacy, and confidentiality.
  
Organize and prioritize multiple assignments and meet established fundraising goals.
  
Maintain accurate donor and prospect records and effectively use advancement CRM systems.
  
Travel and participate in occasional evening and weekend activities as required.
  
Work from Cal Lutheran main campus to PLTS campus/Northern

jobs.title: Director of Fundraising / Development
jobs.description:
**Type:** Full\-time contractor (hours negotiable)

**Location:** Remote, based in the SF Bay Area, Seattle, New York, or Washington, DC (US time zones)

**Travel:** Expectation of 20\-40% travel time between US, EU and India.


OpenFn is the Digital Public Good for public service automation \& AI orchestration. Our platform automates data exchange and digital workflows so that governments and NGOs can deliver public services more efficiently, achieve interoperability across fragmented systems, and scale critical public services across health, humanitarian, and government programs.


Our team, Open Function Group, the primary steward of this open\-source platform, is a lean, fully\-remote team of integration specialists, solution architects, and implementation consultants working across 15\+ countries.


We are not making marginal improvements to already comfortable lives. We are building the digital public infrastructure that allows governments to function, clinics to operate, and vulnerable populations to access services they depend on.


Supporting document (with ideas for fundraising against): https://www.openfn.org/blog/dpi\-ai


The role**We're hiring OpenFn's first Director of Fundraising to lead our organization’s fundraising efforts with major donors, foundations, and mission\-aligned funders who invest in Digital Public Goods, Digital Public Infrastructure, and social\-impact technology. We will always act in the public interest, never for private profit. We want investment which is aligned as such.**


To date, OpenFn's growth has come from delivering complex digital transformation and implementation projects, and from fundraising efforts our CEO has largely driven himself. As we invest more deliberately in philanthropic and institutional funding to complement our subscription revenue, we're looking for an experienced fundraiser to build this function from the ground up: developing a fundraising strategy, cultivating and stewarding relationships with foundations and major donors, and helping OpenFn secure the multi\-year support it needs to keep expanding access to public service automation.


You already have a network of relationships with foundations, funders, and philanthropists active in international development, Digital Public Goods, and technology for social good, and you know how to translate a mission into a compelling case for support. You're comfortable being both the strategist and the one making the ask: this is a foundational hire, so you'll build the playbook as you go rather than inherit one.


We believe some of OpenFn's biggest fundraising opportunities sit at the intersection of philanthropy and policy, for instance helping governments understand why workflow and AI orchestration are essential to resilient digital public infrastructure or articulating the influence that open platforms have on the concentration of power in a market. Prior experience in policy conversations around Digital Public Goods or ICT for Development, and a passion for understanding and addressing the macroeconomic forces that shape wealth inequality is a requirement.


What you'll be doing**Build our fundraising strategy**

* Develop and lead OpenFn's fundraising strategy across major donors, foundations, and other mission\-aligned funders
* Establish the processes, systems, and reporting cadence a growing fundraising function needs, since you will be OpenFn's first dedicated fundraising hire (see helpful pointers from Wayan Vota!)
* Set and track fundraising priorities in partnership with the CEO and leadership team

**Cultivate \& grow major donor and foundation relationships**

* Identify, cultivate, and steward relationships with foundations, family offices, and individual major donors aligned with OpenFn's mission
* Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective funders, from first conversation through multi\-year commitment
* Represent OpenFn credibly and persuasively with senior funder audiences, translating our technical work into a compelling case for impact and support

**Develop compelling funding proposals \& materials**

* Write and coordinate proposals, funding narratives, and reports that clearly connect OpenFn's work to funder priorities
* Partner with the CEO and program teams to gather the impact data and stories that anchor a strong case for support

**Engage the policy \& DPG ecosystem (a plus)**

* Build relationships across the broader Digital Public Goods and Digital Public Infrastructure funding community
* Represent OpenFn in relevant policy conversations and convenings where doing so could unlock new funding relationships

**Report on progress \& sustain funder relationships**

* Track and report on fundraising pipeline, commitments, and funder engagement to the CEO and leadership
* Ensure funders receive timely, high\-quality communications and reporting that keeps them engaged for the long term

  

**Requirements**  

  

Required Qualifications* 10\+ years of experience in fundraising, development, or philanthropic partnerships, ideally within international development, global health, or technology\-for\-good organizations
* A demonstrated network of relationships with foundations, major donors, or other institutional funders active in social impact or technology for development
* A track record of securing significant gifts or grants and stewarding funder relationships over multiple years
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical, mission\-driven work into a compelling case for support for a range of audiences
* Strong project management and organizational skills, comfortable building process where none exists
* Ability to work independently and as part of a small, fully\-remote team
* Fluent, professional\-level English communication skills (written and verbal), with the ability to work effectively across a distributed, multicultural team
* Reliable access to a quiet, dedicated remote workspace with stron

**OVERVIEW**

Capital Strategy Meets Business Growth.

**Are you a strategic relationship builder who knows how to turn opportunity into action—and relationships into capital?**

Do you know how to move comfortably between founders, investors, corporate executives, funders, and strategic partners? Can you identify where capital and opportunity intersect, open the right doors, develop meaningful relationships, and help move high\-value opportunities from conversation to commitment?

If so, this may be your seat at the table.

**JPG Enterprises Consulting (JPGE)** is an emerging, woman\-led enterprise building a diversified ecosystem across strategic growth, capital, executive leadership, real estate, housing innovation, global health and impact, business development, and emerging ventures.

We are seeking a **Director, Partnerships \& Strategic Capital** to help lead the development of JPGE's strategic capital ecosystem—building relationships, partnerships, and capital pathways that support enterprise growth and the activation of high\-value opportunities across the JPGE portfolio.

This is not simply a fundraising role.

It is a **senior strategic growth and capital\-development role** for someone who understands that capital is most powerful when it is aligned with the right opportunity, relationship, structure, and strategic objective.

The Director will work closely with the Founder \& CEO and **Global Capital \& Development Group (GCD)** leadership to identify, cultivate, structure, and advance strategic capital and partnership opportunities across the enterprise.

**THE ROLE**

The Director, Partnerships \& Strategic Capital will lead the development of relationships and opportunities across the intersection of:

**Capital \+ Partnerships \+ Business Development \+ Strategic Growth**

The role is responsible for helping JPGE build a qualified capital pipeline, cultivate high\-value relationships, identify appropriate capital pathways, and convert strategic relationships into actionable opportunities.

The Director will operate at both the **relationship level and the enterprise strategy level**—representing JPGE externally while helping shape the systems, processes, and opportunity architecture required to support scalable capital development.

This includes relationships with investors, family offices, corporate partners, strategic collaborators, financial institutions, institutional funders, and other aligned capital sources.

The Director will lead a small **Partnerships \& Strategic Capital team**, providing strategic direction, coaching, prioritization, and accountability while remaining personally engaged in high\-value external relationship development and capital opportunities.

The Director is expected to be an **originator, strategist, relationship architect, and opportunity developer**—not simply a manager of an existing pipeline.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1\. Strategic Capital Development**

Build and manage a qualified pipeline of strategic capital relationships and opportunities aligned with JPGE's growth priorities.

This may include:

* Private investors
* Family offices
* Corporate capital
* Strategic investment partners
* Institutional capital
* Corporate sponsorships
* Financial and lending relationships
* Strategic financing partners
* Growth\-oriented funding relationships
* Other aligned capital sources

The goal is not simply to generate a large prospect list.

The goal is to build a **high\-quality relationship pipeline capable of producing meaningful strategic opportunities.**

**2\. Strategic Partnership Development**

Identify, cultivate, and develop relationships with organizations and leaders who can contribute more than capital—including:

* Strategic access
* Market entry
* Distribution
* Expertise
* Institutional credibility
* Business development opportunities
* Industry relationships
* Strategic resources
* Co\-development opportunities

Develop partnership concepts that create meaningful mutual value and advance JPGE's broader growth strategy.

**3\. Capital Strategy \& Opportunity Structuring**

Help determine the appropriate capital pathway for emerging opportunities based on:

* Strategic objectives
* Business model
* Capital requirements
* Opportunity readiness
* Risk and complexity
* Partner/investor fit
* Timing
* Growth potential
* Transaction or partnership structure

Potential pathways may include strategic investment, corporate partnerships, sponsorship, institutional financing, debt or alternative financing structures, and other appropriate capital mechanisms.

The Director is not expected to personally execute every financing mechanism; rather, the role requires the ability to **identify, evaluate, coordinate, and advance the appropriate pathway with the necessary internal and external expertise.**

**4\. Convert Relationships Into Strategic Opportunities**

Move relationships through a disciplined progression:

**Relationship → Conversation → Qualified Opportunity → Strategy / Structure → Proposal → Commitment**

Opportunities may include:

* Investment
* Sponsorship
* Strategic partnership
* Financing
* Joint ventures
* Corporate collaboration
* Expansion opportunities
* Capital introductions
* Business development relationships
* Strategic alliances
* Other enterprise\-growth opportunities

The Director will be measured not only by activity, but by the quality and progression of opportunities created.

**5\. Enterprise\-Wide Capital Alignment**

Work across JPGE's ecosystem to understand where capital and strategic relationships can create the greatest value.

This may include collaboration with:

* Global Capital \& Development Group
* Partnerships \& Strategic Capital
* Partnerships \& Strategic Philanthropy
* Real Estate \+ M\&A
* Housing Innovation \& Community Development
* Global Health \& Impact Strategy
* JPGE Leadership Institute for Strategic Growth
* Capital Intelligence Initiative™
* Other JPGE ventures and strategic i

### **Description**

 **ABOUT BREAKTHROUGH NEW YORK**
Breakthrough New York empowers motivated students from low\-income communities to achieve a college degree and reach their fullest potential. Our tuition\-free program supports over 500 students and their families from 7th grade through college. We accept middle school students who are furthest from high\-quality educational opportunities yet show promise and potential: 99% of students identify as persons of color and 56% will be the first in their families to graduate college.  

As a ten\-year program, Breakthrough New York supports students and their families through key transition points in their academic journeys. We provide academic enrichment through summer and after\-school opportunities; coach students to gain admissions into selective high schools and colleges, and expose students to diverse interests and careers so they can shape their own trajectories.  

In addition to nurturing individual talent, we cultivate a thriving community of like\-minded peers and mentors who encourage each other’s ambitions and passions. Personalized mentorship and holistic support are signature elements of our model, with over 200 near\-peer seasonal staff and volunteers who work with students at each stage of our continuum.  

The Breakthrough model works: 94% of Breakthrough students enroll in college preparatory high schools, and 97% are on track to graduate from college in four\-six years. Learn more at Breakthrough New York's website. **ABOUT THE POSITION**
  

*Reporting directly to the Chief Development Officer (CDO), the Director of Grants and Communications Manager will join the development team to collaboratively raise an organizational budget of $4\.024M annually, and oversee a portfolio of $1\.2M \- $1\.5M current and prospective opportunities. jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
Description:
**BACKGROUND**

**The Organization**


Since 1984, STRIVE has helped individuals facing significant barriers to employment gain access to meaningful careers, economic mobility, and long\-term opportunity. Through its proven Five\-Pillar Model, STRIVE combines career readiness, occupational skills training, career coaching, job placement assistance, and lifetime support to help participants secure and sustain employment. Over four decades, STRIVE and its affiliates have served more than 90,000 individuals nationwide.


Today, STRIVE operates direct\-service sites in New York City, Atlanta, Birmingham, New Orleans, Northern New Jersey, and will open a new site in Houston in Spring 2027\. Additionally, STRIVE supports a growing network of partner\-operated programs across the country. The organization has earned national recognition for achieving strong outcomes while serving individuals who face some of the greatest barriers to employment, including housing instability, justice\-system involvement, and substance use recovery.


STRIVE is now embarking on an ambitious next chapter. Guided by a multi\-year growth plan, developed with the support of The Bridgespan Group, the organization aims to serve 20,000 individuals annually by 2036 through a growing network of direct\-operated and partner\-operated sites, positioning STRIVE as the nation's leading employment partner for highly barriered jobseekers. Over the next decade, STRIVE expects to serve approximately 110,000 individuals, generating an estimated $1\.5 billion in wage gains and transforming economic opportunity for families and communities across the country.


To achieve this vision, STRIVE is investing in organizational capacity, fundraising, public funding strategy, technology, evaluation, and national infrastructure. The organization's next Chief Development Officer will play a critical leadership role in securing the resources, partnerships, and strategic investments necessary to fuel this growth and national expansion.


To learn more about STRIVE, please visit www.strive.org

**The Position**


The Chief Development Officer reports to the Chief Executive Officer, serves as a member of STRIVE's Executive Leadership Team, and leads the organization's Development function.


STRIVE enters this search from a position of strength. The organization has built a highly capable fundraising team, established sophisticated development systems and processes, and secured support from many of the nation's leading philanthropic institutions including Ballmer Group, Blue Meridian Partners, and MacKenzie Scott’s Yield Giving. The next Chief Development Officer will focus on accelerating growth, expanding revenue, strengthening organizational positioning, and securing transformational investments that support STRIVE's long\-term vision for national scale.


Over the coming years, STRIVE must demonstrate its ability to expand into new markets, support partner\-operated sites, increase public funding, activate local fundraising ecosystems, and sustain a growing national network. The Chief Development Officer will serve as the architect of that fundraising strategy, translating organizational ambitions into actionable revenue plans and ensuring the organization has the philanthropic, public, and private resources necessary to achieve its goals.


This leader will partner closely with the CEO, Executive Directors, board members, local advisory boards, and external funding partners to identify opportunities, cultivate strategic relationships, and secure transformational investments. The successful candidate will combine strategic vision with disciplined execution, proactively identifying new funding opportunities, mobilizing stakeholders around clear fundraising priorities, and ensuring accountability for results across a complex and growing organization. They will be equally comfortable developing long\-term revenue strategies and driving day\-to\-day progress toward ambitious fundraising goals.

  



**ROLE OVERVIEW**

**Revenue Strategy**

* In partnership with organizational leadership, translate STRIVE’s growth plan into national, regional, and site\-level fundraising strategies, budgets, forecasts, and targets.
* In partnership with Executive Directors, develop strategy and capacity to increase local fundraising and support local sites in achieving self\-sustaining operations over time.
* Coordinate institutional, government, individual, corporate, special event, and other potential revenue sources, while identifying new unrestricted and partnership\-based opportunities.
* Identify and prioritize high\-potential institutional, corporate, government, and philanthropic prospects, developing actionable pursuit strategies that engage executive leadership, board members, and local leaders in successful cultivation efforts.

**About Us:** Acacia Network, the leading Latino integration care nonprofit in the nation, offers the community, from children to seniors, a pathway to behavioral and primary healthcare, housing, and empowerment. We are visionary leaders transforming the triple aim of high quality, and great experience at a lower cost. Acacia champions a collaborative environment to deliver vital health, housing, and community\-building services, work we have been doing since 1969\. jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
The Bruce Museum in Greenwich, Connecticut, seeks a dynamic, experienced, collaborative, and highly creative **Director of Marketing and Communications** to join the senior leadership team led by The Susan E. Lynch Executive Director \& CEO. The DMC is a strategist, content creator, leader and manager of the full range of the Museum’s communications, and a close thought partner to the ED \& CEO. The role brings clarity and focus to work streams critical to the Museum’s success and works alongside peer department leaders to carry it forward.

The Bruce is at an important juncture. With the 2023 completion of a $68 million transformational expansion that tripled gallery space, the Museum is building an integrated art and science identity across its public voice and its visitor experience. Leading that work, the DMC will set strategy for the Museum's brand, grow its audiences, and strengthen attendance, membership, and earned revenue. The DMC also holds a standing seat on the Exhibition Strategy Team and the Programming Strategy Team, ensuring the audience has a voice in decisions about what the Museum presents and when.

**Position Overview:**

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads the Museum’s institutional marketing and communications. The position sets brand and audience strategy, builds the plans that carry it across every platform and visitor touchpoint, and grows audience, membership, and earned revenue. The Director thinks about the full visitor journey, from the first time someone hears of the Bruce, to the decision to come, to the visit itself, to the reason they return and become a member.

Reporting to the ED \& CEO and serving as a member of the senior leadership team, the DMC leads the internal marketing team and directs the Museum’s external communications partner in a unified strategy. The role works across the Museum’s departments to align programming, exhibitions, development, and visitor experience around a coherent institutional voice. The role partners with senior leadership to build the Museum’s reputation with visitors, members, donors, the press, schools, and the wider cultural community regionally and nationally.

The position has two direct reports, including a Marketing Associate and a Digital Media Associate. The position also directs the Museum's external communications consultants.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Brand and Audience Strategy: Set the Museum’s brand positioning and audience strategy, and translate institutional priorities into an institutional marketing plan that advances them. Shape the Bruce’s art and science identity narrative and build recognition across the region and nation.
* Audience Growth: Own the strategy for growing attendance and converting visitors into members. Set annual audience targets in partnership with the ED \& CEO and the COO, build the acquisition and conversion approach behind them, and report performance against them. Earned revenue is a shared institutional goal; marketing owns the path from awareness to attendance to membership that drives it.
* Institutional Strategy: Serve on the Exhibition Strategy Team and the Programming Strategy Team, bringing audience evidence into exhibition planning, scheduling, and program design.
* Integrated Marketing: Oversee institutional, exhibition, programmatic, and fundraising marketing plans across advertising, digital, email, social media, and print. Partner with Audience Engagement, Development, and Curatorial Affairs to craft compelling campaigns and maintain brand consistency across all platforms and visitor touchpoints.
* Digital Platforms: Own strategy and performance for the Museum's website, email, and social platforms, and ensure they work together to move people from awareness to attendance to membership.
* Audience Research and Analytics: Lead audience research and use data to guide decisions. Track performance and test new approaches. Know who is coming to the Museum, who is not, and what would change that.
* Public Relations: Lead the Museum’s regional and national media strategy, working in partnership with the Museum’s external communications agency. Build relationships with press covering art, science, and culture. Manage the Museum’s reputation, anticipate issues before they surface, and direct crisis communications, establishing messaging and approval pathways so the Museum can respond quickly and clearly.
* Team and Budget Leadership: Lead and develop the marketing team. Build and manage the marketing and communications budget with the Chief Operating Officer and other peers, aligning budget with institutional priorities. Oversee the Museum’s agencies and vendors and direct spending where it can most effectively drive audience and revenue.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Five or more years of experience leading marketing for an institution or mission\-driven enterprise, with a trajectory and results that demonstrate readiness for this scope. While Museum experience is not required, fluency with art, science, and ideas is essential.
* Bachelor’s degree. Background in the arts, humanities, education, or related field is welcome.
* An exceptional storyteller and editor. Able to write clearly, shape a narrative, and serve as a public voice for the Museum.
* Track record of growing audience, revenue, and engagement through strategy and disciplined execution, with the analytical rigor to turn awareness into attendance and attendance into membership. Able to set targets, test approaches, and measure results.
* Experience leading a team and directing agency and consultant partners towards a cohesive strategy.
* Strong command of digital marketing, CRM systems, and audience analytics. Able to use data to understand visitors, identify new audiences, and guide decisions.
* Skilled at positioning an organization with media, civic and business leaders, cultural peers, and the general public. Familiarity with a wide range of media channels appropriate for disseminati

jobs.description:
Pace University seeks an outstanding philanthropy professional and proficient team leader for a senior role as the Associate Vice President of Development (AVP) empowered to develop and execute multi\-year campaign strategies to build a robust pipeline of individual donors and prospects for the University. The position will work across all of the University’s schools and programs: Lubin School of Business, Dyson College of Arts and Sciences, Seidenberg School of Computer Science and Information Systems, College of Health Professions, Elisabeth Haub School of Law, and Sand College of Performing Arts. This individual will be responsible for developing charitable giving programs with a focus on major gifts and managing the frontline fundraising strategies to significantly expand financial resources available to the University. The Associate VP will oversee the strategy and execution on the University’s priorities for growing contributed revenue including its current $300M comprehensive campaign — now nearing a successful close — focused on scholarships, capital projects, programs and centers, the Haub Law School, and Sands College of Performing Arts. The successful candidate will be expected to play a leading role in completing the campaign and directing post\-campaign activities, including final solicitations, close\-phase stewardship, donor recognition and transition to long\-term stewardship and future campaign planning.

  



The Associate VP will oversee the strategy and execution on the University’s priorities for growing contributed revenue including its current comprehensive campaign focused on scholarships, capital projects, the Haub Law School, and performing arts programs. The Associate VP will also manage a prospect portfolio of 75\-100 individuals and will be responsible for personally soliciting major gifts of $100,000 or more. The role will work closely with the Vice President of Development and Alumni Relations (VP) to evaluate regional and international fundraising strategies. The role will be responsible for driving departmental fundraising results and formulating/enforcing major gift policies and procedures for the department. The role will partner with the VP and DEVAR’s senior leaders to create volunteer engagement strategies to maximize potential support from alumni, parents, and University friends. The Associate VP will serve as a senior member of the Office to Development and Alumni Relations and will collaborate closely with all areas of the office to advance the major gift program. This position reports to the Vice President of Development and Alumni Relations.

  


**Position Duties**


* Retain, hire, manage, and mentor a team of high\-performing major gift officers organized around school teams including Lubin, Dyson, Seidenberg, CHP, Haub Law, and Sands.
* Working closely with the VP to ensure the Pace campaign case resonates with donors and propels increased giving.
* Effectively use qualitative and quantitative data to analyze the major giving gift teams’ performance, assess current and future potential, and scan the environment for the most recent trends on philanthropy.
* Provides direct guidance to the major gift team as it continues to grow and mature, combining the best elements of the art and science of fundraising practice.
* Effectively manages a portfolio of individual donors and prospects, primarily those rated as capable of giving at the level of $100,000 and more.
* Works closely with a variety of Pace stakeholders including providing leadership to the Schools individual Advisory Boards, and Parents \& Family Council. These groups should be effective tools in support of increased giving, meaningful volunteer experiences, and improve opportunities for Pace students. Along with the Vice President, serve as the Campaign Director, advocate, and spokesperson.
* Enhances Pace’s ability to integrate donors and potential donors into the Pace community and engages new and existing constituents nationally and internationally.
* Networks and connects regularly with donors and prospective donors, building and sustaining their positive relationships with Pace, as well as securing and pursuing related leads.
* In collaboration with the Vice President for Advancement and Associate Vice President for Alumni and Constituent Experiences, help to determine the direction of the University’s stewardship and donor relations program to recognize donors in effective and meaningful ways.
* Through supervision of the Director of Planned Giving, create planned gift acquisition strategies and develop stewardship strategies for current planned giving donors.
* Develop strong positive relationships with the Pace community to establish Development and Alumni Relations as Pace’s major resource and coordinator for all University fundraising.
* In consultation with the Vice President, the AVP will establish and adhere to annual operating budgets and ensures that Pace’s philanthropy programs are operating in a fiscally prudent and productive way.
* Keep abreast of current best practices in the advancement/development profession and evaluates new and emerging ideas for potential implementation. Help develop and administer Pace’s policies related to fundraising and gift stewardship.
* Effectively utilize the office’s CRM to record prospect/donor activity and other relevant data in a timely fashion.
* Exceptional communication skills to include effective and persuasive writing, public speaking, and interpersonal skills and must display extraordinary tact and satisfy the donor/prospect while maintaining the integrity of Pace.
* Be prepared and stand ready at all times to represent the VP and/or University President, in meetings with donors, prospects, and alumni audiences.
* Foster collaborative relationships with peers within the Development department to establish a cohesive team strategy across giving channels that will ensure coordinated donor cultivation toward ongoing revenue g

jobs.title: Executive Director
Director of Operations at Hope House
jobs.description:
**About Hope House**

Hope House is a nonprofit organization providing transitional housing for homeless families in the Wolfeboro, NH area. Hope House has seven bedroom units with private bathrooms plus a shared kitchen and living space. In addition to housing, Hope House helps connect its tenants with various social services including job placement and mental health support, with the ultimate goal of helping families move toward stable, independent housing. The average length of stay at Hope House is 110 days.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations is responsible for the safe, consistent, and effective day\-to\-day operation of Hope House. This person will lead a small team, maintain staffing coverage for a 24/7 residential program, support strong occupancy, and ensure that families receive respectful, well\-coordinated assistance during their stay. The role combines residential operations, staff supervision, community partnership development, problem\-solving, and resident\-service coordination. The Director of Operations will help create an environment that is orderly, welcoming, accountable, and focused on helping families progress toward stable housing.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Manage the day\-to\-day operation of Hope House and ensure consistent, safe, reliable coverage for a 24/7 residential setting.
* Recruit, schedule, train, supervise, coach, and evaluate approximately 4\-6 staff members; maintain appropriate coverage for evenings, weekends, holidays, and staff absences.
* Implement Hope House policies, procedures, resident expectations, safety practices, confidentiality standards, and incident\-response protocols.
* Oversee intake, move\-in, occupancy, unit turnover, and move\-out processes, with a goal of using available housing capacity effectively and appropriately.
* Maintain accurate operational and resident records and establish practical systems for documentation, handoffs, and internal communication.
* Build relationships with referral sources and community partners to support a healthy pipeline of eligible families.
* Coordinate access to community\-based services for residents, including employment and job\-placement assistance, mental\-health services, benefits navigation, education, childcare, transportation, and other supports as available.
* Help families connect with longer\-term housing resources and other services that support successful transitions out of Hope House.
* Develop working partnerships with local social\-service agencies, healthcare and behavioral\-health providers, schools, employers, housing organizations, and other community resources.
* Monitor household needs, supplies, maintenance needs, and other operational concerns; escalate significant risks promptly.
* Track basic operating expenses and support budget management, purchasing controls, and financial reporting in coordination with the Executive Director.
* Collect and report practical program information such as occupancy, referrals, length of stay, service connections, incidents, exits, and other measures established by Hope House Executive Director and Board of Directors.
* Provide regular operational updates to the Executive Director and support reports to the Board as requested.
* Participate in an on\-call or escalation structure appropriate for a 24/7 program; this does not mean the Director is personally expected to work around the clock.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* At least 5 years of experience in residential services, housing, social services, human services, nonprofit operations, or a related field.
* Experience supervising staff and managing schedules in an operation that requires dependable coverage.
* Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities in a dynamic environment.
* Sound judgment and the ability to respond calmly and appropriately to conflicts, emergencies, and sensitive situations.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to collaborate with families, staff, community organizations, and service providers.
* Experience building referral networks or coordinating social\-service resources is strongly preferred.
* Familiarity with trauma\-aware, strengths\-based, or family\-centered approaches is preferred.
* Comfort with basic data tracking, documentation, expense management, and operational reporting.

**Success in the Role**

The Director of Operations will be successful when:

* Hope House is consistently staffed, safe, well organized, appropriately occupied, and connected to a dependable network of community services.
* When families experience clear expectations, responsive support, and effective connections to resources that help them move toward stable housing.

Pay: $59,777\.27 \- $89,946\.82 per year

Benefits:

jobs.description:
**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**

**Storehouse West, Inc. \- Rio Rancho, New Mexico**

**Part\-Time \| 25 Hours per Week \| $40,800 Annual Salary**

Storehouse West is seeking a compassionate, energetic, and community\-minded leader to serve as our next Executive Director.

Storehouse West is a community\-focused nonprofit organization serving residents of Sandoval County who are in need. We provide nourishing food, children's clothing, assistance with utility bills, and referrals to other community resources.

Our Executive Director is the day\-to\-day leader of the organization and works closely with our Board of Directors, employees, volunteers, donors, and community partners to carry out the Storehouse West mission.

The Position

The Executive Director is the chief administrative, supervisory, and development officer of Storehouse West and reports directly to the Board of Directors.

This is a 25\-hour\-per\-week position, with the Executive Director expected to be present during all Storehouse West office and food\-distribution hours. The position also requires attendance at monthly Board meetings and participation in community activities, including Chamber of Commerce events and meetings with current and prospective donors. Some of these responsibilities may occasionally take place outside regular Storehouse West office hours.

This is very much a hands\-on leadership position. We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people and is just as comfortable talking with a donor or community leader as working alongside our employees and volunteers to solve an everyday operational problem.

What You'll Do

· Manage the day\-to\-day operations of the organization and oversee our food, children's clothing, utility\-assistance, and referral programs.

· Lead and support our paid staff and volunteers, including recruiting, training, supervision, performance management, and recognition.

· Work with the Board to develop organizational priorities, plans, policies, and budgets.

· Provide the Board with timely, accurate, and complete information needed to fulfill its governance and oversight responsibilities.

· Maintain strong professional relationships with Roadrunner Food Bank, food\-rescue partners, donors, churches, businesses, government agencies, and other community organizations.

· Develop and carry out an annual fundraising plan in partnership with the Fund Development Committee.

· Seek grants, donations, sponsorships, and other financial and in\-kind support.

· Develop and maintain relationships with major donors while building a sustainable base of individual donors.

· Oversee fundraising events, donor records, proposals, and required reports.

· Work with the Finance Committee and Board to maintain sound financial practices and operate within the Board\-approved budget.

· Maintain organizational records and help ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements.

· Oversee Storehouse West facilities and equipment and maintain a safe, clean environment.

· Represent Storehouse West throughout the community and help increase awareness of our mission.

· Support our website, social media, newsletters, annual report, and other community communications.

· Attend Board meetings, provide regular Executive Director reports, and work cooperatively with the Board and its committees.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who genuinely cares about serving people and understands that the success of a community nonprofit depends on relationships \- with clients, employees, volunteers, donors, community partners, and the Board.

**Strong candidates will have:**

· Experience in nonprofit leadership, management, community service, or a related field.

· Experience supervising employees and working with volunteers.

· Fundraising, donor\-development, or grant\-writing experience.

· Strong organizational, communication, leadership, and problem\-solving skills.

· The ability to build and maintain productive community partnerships.

· An understanding of budgeting and basic nonprofit financial management.

· Computer proficiency, including word processing, email, internet/social media, and familiarity with financial\-management software such as QuickBooks.

· The ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently while also being an effective member of a team.

· The ability to work effectively with and report to a nonprofit Board of Directors.

A bachelor's degree in business, public relations, nonprofit management, or a related field is preferred. Significant relevant leadership and management experience may be considered in place of a degree.

Experience with food\-assistance programs, food banks, nonprofit compliance, fundraising, grant development, or service on or with a nonprofit Board is also highly desirable.

Compensation and Schedule

**Salary:** $40,800 annually ($3,400 per month)

**Schedule:** Approximately 25 hours per week

**Location:** Rio Rancho, New Mexico

**Benefits:** This position does not currently include employee benefits.

The Executive Director is expected to be present during Storehouse West office/distribution hours and attend monthly Board meetings. The position also includes occasional community, Chamber of Commerce, donor, and fundraising activities outside normal office hours.

How to Apply

Interested candidates should submit:

· A current resume

· A cover letter explaining their interest in Storehouse West and the Executive Director position

· Professional references

**Applications should be submitted to: executivedirector@storehousewest.org**

The position will remain open until filled. Applications will be reviewed as they are received.

***Storehouse West, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer.***

Pay: From $40,800\.00 per year

Work Location: In person
