### **What We Can Achieve Together:**

  

The Associate Director of Development (ADoD) is an experienced “out the door” fundraiser and self\-starter with excellent writing skills who excels as a collaborative team member who brings leadership to their portfolio and fundraising strategies. The ADoD develops, implements, and plans for the cultivation and solicitation of gift prospects, primarily individual donors and potential corporate, foundation, and institutional funders. This person will be part of a team that is driven, strategic and thoughtful. This role is ideal for a strategic fundraiser who enjoys identifying, qualifying, and building relationships with new major donor prospects while also managing a portfolio of established donors to contribute to the ongoing mission of our global conservation work.  



  

### **We’re Looking for You:**

  

The Associate Director of Development for The Nature Conservancy in Maine is based out of our Brunswick, Maine office and is responsible for managing a portfolio of qualified donors and for building strong relationships. The ADoD promotes a culture of philanthropy among their peers and volunteers and works closely with the development team, Advisory Board of Trustees, natural partners, and other Conservancy staff to determine effective strategies for engaging identified donors and prospects and deepening their relationships with The Nature Conservancy. This person inspires by telling stories about the Conservancy’s work and ably connects donors to their values.  



The ADoD understands and applies complex principles of developing donor strategies and builds strong relationships with a portfolio of prospects, as well as new and current donors. They are an experienced, creative and strategic fundraiser driven by donor interest and energized by pipeline discovery and qualification. The successful candidate will be highly collaborative and bring a track record of delivering results. As part of a 9\-person team, this role focuses largely on discovery and qualification towards building a high\-value portfolio. They are responsible for direct asks for both global and local Conservancy priorities to meet funding needs. They discuss assets proficiently and listen for opportunities for gifts of assets or other non\-cash gifts, such as planned gifts and gifts of real estate or trade lands. They incorporate blended gifts and gifts of assets in proposals to donors. They understand organizational budgets and are proficient in utilizing this knowledge to build proposal budgets. They will work collaboratively across chapters and programs with a spirit of “One Conservancy” and leverage institutional knowledge and networks for successful and sophisticated donor strategies. They work closely with chapter leadership (including the State Director and Director of Conservation) and manage assigned trustee relationships and/or volunteer engagement. They are required to use the Conservancy’s donor database and collaborate with team members who plan events, donor stewardship, and written communications.  



  

**RESPONSIBILITIES \& SCOPE**

* Manage a portfolio of 80 – 120 individual and corporate/foundation donors, including donors with the capacity to give over $250,000, once the portfolio is developed (composition of portfolio to include 30\-40%\+ in discovery and 10%\+ in loyal donor outreach). Once the portfolio has fully matured, meet an annual fundraising goal of $1,000,000 or more, along with a goal for bequest notifications.

OpenFn is the Digital Public Good for public service automation \& AI orchestration. Our platform automates data exchange and digital workflows so that governments and NGOs can deliver public services more efficiently, achieve interoperability across fragmented systems, and scale critical public services across health, humanitarian, and government programs.


Our team, Open Function Group, the primary steward of this open\-source platform, is a lean, fully\-remote team of integration specialists, solution architects, and implementation consultants working across 15\+ countries.


We are not making marginal improvements to already comfortable lives. We are building the digital public infrastructure that allows governments to function, clinics to operate, and vulnerable populations to access services they depend on.


Supporting document (with ideas for fundraising against): https://www.openfn.org/blog/dpi\-ai


The role**We're hiring OpenFn's first Director of Fundraising to lead our organization’s fundraising efforts with major donors, foundations, and mission\-aligned funders who invest in Digital Public Goods, Digital Public Infrastructure, and social\-impact technology. We will always act in the public interest, never for private profit. We want investment which is aligned as such.**


To date, OpenFn's growth has come from delivering complex digital transformation and implementation projects, and from fundraising efforts our CEO has largely driven himself. As we invest more deliberately in philanthropic and institutional funding to complement our subscription revenue, we're looking for an experienced fundraiser to build this function from the ground up: developing a fundraising strategy, cultivating and stewarding relationships with foundations and major donors, and helping OpenFn secure the multi\-year support it needs to keep expanding access to public service automation.


You already have a network of relationships with foundations, funders, and philanthropists active in international development, Digital Public Goods, and technology for social good, and you know how to translate a mission into a compelling case for support. new_jobs.title: Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
Leukemia Texas is seeking a visionary and passionate Executive Director to lead our

organization in its mission of helping Texans beat leukemia, through patient aid, research,

and innovation. Leukemia includes a variety of blood cancers that affect people of all ages,

from very young children to the elderly.

**Executive Director Responsibilities:**

*○ Provide strategic direction and oversight for all aspects of the organization.*

*○ Develop and implement a comprehensive long\-term plan to achieve Leukemia Texas'*

*mission.*

*○ Lead the Board of Directors and ensure effective governance.*

*○ Oversee all staff, volunteers, fundraising events, and programs to ensure efficient and*

*impactful operations.*

Patient Advocacy:

*○ Champion the needs of patients and their families by securing resources and programs*

*to provide support throughout their treatment journey.*

*○ Ensure strong relationships with healthcare providers and patient advocacy groups.*

Development:

*○ Lead the organization in securing financial support through individual donors, corporate*

*sponsors, 3rd party fundraisers and foundations.*

*○ Develop and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy, including grant writing,*

*management of special events, including the annual Beat Leukemia Ball, and creation of*

*new opportunities.*

*○ Oversee all fundraising activities and ensure achievement of annual fundraising goals.*

*○ Build and maintain strong relationships with major donors and cultivate new giving*

*opportunities.*

Financial Management:

*○ Work collaboratively with the Leukemia Texas Board of Directors to develop and monitor*

*the organization's annual budget.*

*○ Provide oversight of our accounting and tax partners to ensure accurate and timely*

*financial reporting to the Board of Directors and compliance with state and federal*

*requirements for a 501(c)(3\) tax exempt non\-profit organization.*

*○ Manage day\-to\-day financials, including banking relationships, cash flow, accounts*

*payable, patient aid grants, and the organization’s risk management.*

Community Engagement:

○ *Represent Leukemia Texas at community events and offer educational programs to*

*raise awareness about leukemia research and patient support services.*

*○ Develop and strengthen partnerships with other organizations to maximize impact.*

**Executive Director Qualifications:**

● Minimum 3\-5 years of experience in a leadership role within the non\-profit sector, with a

proven track record of success in fundraising, program development, special events, and

financial and budget management. Strategic thinker with ability to develop and implement

a long\-term vision.

● Strong understanding of the non\-profit fundraising landscape in Texas.

● Experience in grant writing and foundation relationships.

● Experience working with a Board of Directors and volunteers.

● Experience with large scale events.

● Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate

a team. Bilingual skills an asset, but not required.

● Passion for the mission of Leukemia Texas and a commitment to making a difference in

the lives of patients and their families.

Benefits:

● Competitive compensation and negotiable benefits, including 401K. Potential for annual

bonus.

● Hybrid work schedule and flexible hours.

● Opportunity to lead a mission\-driven organization and make a real impact in the fight to

Beat Leukemia.

● Work in a fast\-paced and rewarding environment.

● Be part of a dedicated and passionate team.

To Apply: Please submit your resume, a cover letter, and names of 2\-3 references to

info@LeukemiaTexas.org Leukemia Texas is an equal opportunity employer.

Pay: $95,000\.00 \- $105,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Dallas, TX 75247

new_jobs.title: Hospital CEO
new_jobs.description:
At Oceans Behavioral Hospital Waco, healing is our focus. We are passionate about helping adults and seniors manage the challenges associated with anxiety, depression and other mental health issues. Utilizing proven, innovative and progressive therapies, our qualified professionals strive to promote long\-term wellness through a range of inpatient and outpatient psychiatric counseling and treatment options.

  


**Benefits We Offer:**


Medical, Dental, Vision Coverage (Multiple Plan Options) \- Eligible first of the month after 30 days.


401 (k) Retirement Savings Plan with Discretionary Company Match


Tuition Reimbursement


Daily Pay


Paid Time Off


Competitive Market Compensation


Short Term Disability, Long Term Disability


Life Insurance


Employee Assistance Program

  


The Hospital Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the overall leadership and operation of the facility’s services, departments, budget and functions, subject to oversight by the Board of Directors. The Hospital Chief Executive Officer directs the ongoing mission and philosophy of care of the facility by demonstrating leadership through exploring, developing, accepting and implementing new ideas with vision, foresight, and customer sensitivity to meet the facility’s and community’s needs. The Hospital Chief Executive Officer shall assure the facility is adequately staffed, programming standards are met and adequate resources are provided to meet the needs of the patient populations served. The Hospital Chief Executive Officer is responsible for the facility’s financial performance, overseeing departmental and committee activity, coordinating efforts to established facility/committee goals, strategic planning, performance improvement planning, marketing and community liaison activities in adherence with the facility policy and procedures, compliance plan, and all internal and external regulatory bodies that apply to the daily operation of the facility. All duties to be done in accordance with Joint Commission, Federal and State regulations, Oceans Behavioral Mission, policies and procedures and Performance Improvement Standards.

  


**Essential Functions:**


* Managing the overall operation of the Hospital, with responsibility to the Governing Board, including control, utilization, and conservation of its physical and financial assets.


* Review and advise in the preparation of annual budget showing the hospital's expected receipts and expenditures; responsible for the supervision of all business affairs and to ensure that all expenditures are controlled to the best possible advantage.


* Managing the ongoing functions of the Hospital by recruiting, employing, and directing adequate numbers of appropriate trained professional and auxiliary personnel, including delegating duties appropriately;


* Submits monthly reports showing the professional service and financial activities of the hospital and prepares and submits such special reports as may be required by the Governing Body.


* Assisting the Governing Body in formulating policy by preparing and presenting to and reviewing with the Governing Body (i) long\-term and short\-term plans of the Hospital, (ii) reports on the nature and extent of funding and other available resources, (iii) reports describing the Hospital's operations, (iv) reports evaluating the efficiency and effectiveness of the Hospital or its program activity, and (v) budgets and financial statements.


* To attend, or have his designated representative attend, all meetings of the Medical Staff; name hospital departmental representatives to Medical Staff committees, when appropriate, and when requested by the Medical Staff. Cooperates with the Medical Staff and to secure like cooperation on the part of all those concerned with the rendering of professional service to the end that the best possible care may be rendered to all patients.


* Complies with Federal and State statutes and regulations in the performance of his/her duties; Assures that appropriate policies, plans and goals are effectively communicated to all staff members.


* Determine which care, treatment or services are provided directly and which are provided through consultation, contract or other agreement.


* Assures that leadership assesses patient flow issues within the hospital, the impact on patient safety and mitigation of that impact.


* Performs other related duties as assigned.



**Requirements**

**Education / Experience:**


* A minimum of a Master’s Degree, with the undergraduate or graduate degree in a Behavioral Services, Administration or a related health care field.
* Must possess one of the following: (1\) Master's Degree and at least three years of full time experience in progressively responsible management positions in healthcare or (2\) a Baccalaureate Degree and at least five years of full time experience in progressively responsible management positions in healthcare or (3\) at least ten years of full time experience in hospital administration.

  




**Qualifications / Skills:**


* Must be a sound leader who possesses excellent communication and interpersonal skills to foster cooperation across departmental lines and manage information, environmental and fiscal resources to accomplish goals.
* Must be able to maintain and demonstrate a broad knowledge of tasks and assets necessary to accomplish the company objectives.
* Must have knowledge about needs and requirements of third party payers and the ability to be culturally sensitive to diverse groupings of employees and consumers of services as well as maintain knowledge.
* Must be continually be up\-to\-date on State, Federal regulations; The Joint Commission regulations, etc.
* Must successfully complete CPR certification and an Oceans approved behavioral health de\-escalation program.

  




**Work Environment:**


Subject to many interruptions. Occasional pressure due to multiple calls and inquiries. This position can be high pace
